utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, who will be responsible for bringing in the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness is just outside in the corridor and if the usher could bring in witness U, please, who is the first Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. ^^ Witness U, called.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a witness with facial distortion and open session and the pseudonym of U.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I appreciate the listing. Perhaps we need to talk with you about this in closed session. We are having some difficulty following, and I just want to make sure that I understand who will be the next witness and what type of protective measures. But thank you for telling me. Let us see if we can get some advance notice so that the Judges will at know at least for the day what to expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being handed to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as witness U is in open session as well, the blinds on this side of the Court should now be raised.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Witness, you will be known in Court as witness U as a pseudonym for your name. Can you tell the Court that you have lived in Kozarac before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before the conflict, how long had you lived in Kozarac for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I lived there for 42 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have a job in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we could have a look at that on a map so we can put it in our mind? D13, please, if that could be put before the witness? I have additional copies of this for your Honours, and it might be useful, as it is planned to be used by the Defence on many occasions, if rather than seeing it on the monitor you have your own copy of D13. (Handed). There is a good suggestion here that if one goes on the overhead projector as well. Witness, if you could just look at that plan of the Kozarac area that I have put before you, do you see [redacted] on the plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you just point to that plan on the overhead projector to your right and mark there [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you live actually at that part of [redacted] or nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in a part of [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you a married man in Kozarac before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What nationality was your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have a son.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he live with you or live away from home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With me, with me, he lived and worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know the Tadic family in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how many years had you known Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would say 30 years at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What other members of his family did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I know his whole family, his father, his mother, brothers. I know all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How often before the conflict did you see Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, I used to see him almost every day, because whenever I went out into the field I would pass by his house, and then when he opened his coffee bar I frequented it. I saw him every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of cafe bar did he open? What sort of people went there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was frequented by all sorts of people, by people of all origins, Croats and Muslims and Serbs. They all frequented his coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did it have any sort of reputation as being a Serb meeting place, people from Serb background, whether they used that instead of other coffee bars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, I never heard anything along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you politically involved in any way before the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you a member of any of the political parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you do your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What years did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In what capacity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in engineering service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The part of Kozarac where you lived [redacted], what was the makeup of the families in your area in terms of ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Serbs, Croats and two or three Muslim households.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recollect the time when Kozarac was shelled in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what date that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 24th May, around 5 past 2 or 10 past 2 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you at that time when that shelling happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day I was at home [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In your home with you at that time was who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were my wife, my brother and my sister-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where was your son at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My son was in Prijedor. He had gone there eight days before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When this shelling happened, did you know it was going to happen? Did you have any warning that anything like that would take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not, and I was confident that there would be no shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware of an ultimatum that had been given by the authorities in Prijedor to the police in Kozarac concerning the handing up of weapons to the civil authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have any involvement in matters relating to that ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know what the deadline was for the ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Sunday, Sunday noon, I think that was the deadline.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When the shelling of Kozarac took place, how did you react? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I went up to shelter, to a stream called Hokovac, there were some summer cottages, and so I went there with my wife and other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at the map that is in front of you which shows Kozarac [redacted], can you tell us roughly in which district it was that you went to where these summer cottages were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here were these cottages, next to the bridge, to the right, some 150 metres from the bridge to the right, roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did other people also go to that area where you went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They came from Kozarac, civilians, women and children, they came up there to that shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About how many people, are you able to say if you can, came out of Kozarac to that area where you were and took shelter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There must have been not less than 2,000 to 3,000 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How soon after the shelling started was it that you left your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May 27th it was when I left [redacted] in the morning at 7 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I can take you back to the start of the shelling on 24th May and you told us about going to the area where the summer cottages were, was it a few hours before you moved out of your home or did you move out of your home straightaway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it could have been about one or two hours later that I went up there to that shelter, rather, to those summer cottages.[redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where you took shelter, were there other families with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there were Muslims and Serbs and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you able to see what was happening down in Kozarac from this place where you were taking shelter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, it was -- one could not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you able to tell in any way where the shelling was coming from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it came from Prijedor, I think, according to what other people said and, judging by shells, they must have been fired from the direction of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having taken shelter in this area of the weekend cottages, did you return to your home at all, or did you just stay there in the shelter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed in the shelter. I did not go back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect how long the shelling continued for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was Sunday, then Monday and Tuesday, three days. It went on for three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So would that be until 26th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, until the 26th May, until the 27th May, I think it was around 4 o'clock in the morning of 27th May that the shelling stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us at all about the kind of shelling, the amount of bombardment, that was taking place? How frequent were the guns firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What type they were, I do not know, but it would go on for about one hour or two, and then there would be a lull again of about one hour or two and then would start again, but what type, what calibres, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At what stage did you leave that shelter where you had taken refuge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left it on 27th May '92 around 7 o'clock in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did others leave the area where you were in at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know if other people had left the area before you did on 27th May at 7 o'clock in the morning, had others moved out from the area where you were taking refuge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some left on 26th May towards half past 7, 8 o'clock in the evening and they went in the -- towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any information or message passed that let people know about moving out of the region and moving down into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, policemen, Muslims who came up there on 26th May, they came up there, they told us to do withdraw towards Kozarac and some people did. We did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The area that you had taken shelter in near [redacted] and [redacted] itself, was that affected by any shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three shells fell there and by accident, it was not shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So leaving the area where you had taken refuge on 27th May, about how many other people left at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We started from [redacted], perhaps around 100, and as we went towards Kozarac there must have been 200 or 300 people amassed because as we were moving so we were being joined by women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where were those other people joining you from, where had they been taking refuge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This movement of people from [redacted], did it form a column which people added to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts, as this column approached Kozarac, were you in the column? Were you at the front, the back or in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, somewhere towards the front of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were people taking any possessions with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some bags perhaps, some clothes, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any transport in the column or were people just walking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Walking, on foot. There were no vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, were there different nationalities in this column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What nationalities were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were Muslims, Croats and there were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What Serb people did you know in the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I knew them. There was my neighbour, [redacted], her mother, [redacted] and others. [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you first see any military personnel in the Kozarac area as you moved in this column from [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw at the entrance to Kozarac by the Mutnik Mosque there were soldiers there, about two kilometres from [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect how many there were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see very many of them, perhaps 20 or 30. They were standing on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What type of soldiers were they? Were they regular army or irregular troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the Yugoslav Army. I did not see any paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect how those troops were dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were all sorts of uniforms. Some were in camouflage uniforms. Others were in those old SMB uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you saw those soldiers near Mutnik, how did they, as you were able to see it, treat the people coming down in the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They behaved decently. They did not harass us, nobody beat us, nobody touched us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having arrived at Mutnik Mosque, whereabouts did your column go in Kozarac? What route did it take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went down the Marsala Tita Street, the High Street, towards the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which school is that in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Elementary school, Rade Kondic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts is that in relation to the layout of Kozarac, the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that is at the bottom, at the end of the street, as you come out of Kozarac, at the very end, at the intersection for the old route to Prijedor and Kamicani, the old road to Banja Luka, at the crossroads itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to look at a photograph and this I will offer to the Court as D55, your Honour. Witness, that is a photograph there, or a series of photographs, that have been put together and do you recognise what that photograph is showing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see. It is the Marsala Tita Street. You can see the school. You can see the fountain. You can see the house of Bosko Dragicevic and his shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has been served on the Prosecution in advance. It is something that is unsuitable to put on the monitor because of its size. There is a copy for each of your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 55 will be admitted. Mr. Kay, I do not have my microphone on. I want to ask you about a reference to a neighbour. Is there a redaction needed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not have my microphone on since the Defence is dealing with this procedure. I am just enquiring.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not think there is in relation to that name. Mr. Wladimiroff will confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have made notes and afterwards I think I will pass it because otherwise we will break each time again.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have a half hour, you know, to handle that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, I know. So far, nothing has happened that we are really worried.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 55 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think you have just told us that that is the photograph of the part of Kozarac where the school is, the Rade Kondic school, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the fountain in the middle and you refer to someone's shop and house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that your column came down into this part of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where exactly did it go, having arrived down here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went towards the Banja Luka/Prijedor road or the intersection on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the new highway, as it is called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Prijedor/Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this stage are you able to tell us how long this column of people in which you were placed stretched? How long it was or the number of people in that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to my assessment, between 2 and a half and 3,000 men, women and children moving along the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can you just tell us in which direction in this photograph is the Banja Luka/Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I certainly will. If we look at the photograph, witness, and we look at the left-hand side where you refer to someone's shop and house ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Answer not translated].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, if we pass down that road, would that ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My neighbour, Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We did not get the translation. I think the concern is were they moving from left to right, in other words, does the photo show the beginning and then going down, right to left?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will take it in stages and it is my mistake. If we look at this photograph, witness, on the right-hand side of the photograph we see behind some trees a building, the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the school, Rade Kondic school, in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the school is there. You can just see the monument in front of the school next to the fountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if you could take us on this photograph then from the right-hand side -- no, the right-hand side, perhaps move your finger to the right-hand side of the photograph, yes, right to the end of the photograph, please. Yes. That is the left, to the other end of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. If you look at the right-hand side of the photograph and just tell us along this photograph, as we look at it in sections, what parts of Kozarac are shown on the photograph? Starting at the right-hand side, yes, there. What building is behind those trees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see some buildings. I think that is the old hospital here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then up here, I think is the cake shop, and then Toma Dobric's house, then the fountain, then the monument in front of the school, of Rade Kondic school, and then the house of Bosko Dragicevic and his shop can be seen on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at this photograph, which side of the photograph, right or left, would it be that Marsala Tita Street comes down into the triangle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at that, the middle of the photograph, looking across the triangle, we see a road, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the one here, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Is it not possible at all to have it on the Elmo? We are having difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We will try that. I understand, your Honour. Perhaps if we could switch the Elmo on and the witness take a position closer to the Elmo as, unfortunately, it is difficult to do. Just leave the photograph there for the moment. Put the pointer at the edge of the photograph on the right, there. Is it right that there is a road that leads down into this area of Kozarac from the right there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which street is that that comes down from the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a bit unclear to me. I think it is the road leading to Kalate, to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think I will abandon this exercise, your Honour!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We can come back to it, perhaps, after the recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I thought the witness had familiarised himself with the photographs, but it does not matter. There we are. If you switch the monitor off and let us go back to the map, D13? You have the map there in front of you, witness. We have looked at [redacted]. You have the map in front of you and we have looked at [redacted]. Can you see Mutnik on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you can keep your finger on the map so it keeps still? Can you just indicate by using that pointer the route that you took from [redacted] down into the centre of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went from [redacted] along this way, along Marsala Tita Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just stop there for a moment. Where you have kept your pointer there, we can see a triangle on the map, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those photographs that I just showed you, were they of that place on the map, the triangle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Just so that we have this in mind, about what time did you arrive at this part of Kozarac, where the triangle is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around 8.15 or 8.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us about troops. You can take your pointer off the triangle for the moment and I will deal with some other matters. You told us about some troops that you had seen near Mutnik. Did you see any other troops or military as you went down Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you arrived at the triangle, did you see any military presence there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of military was there there? What sort of equipment and men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw people in uniform, camouflage uniform and in Yugoslav SMB uniforms. They had automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see stay for any time down there at the triangle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we stayed there for about one and a half or two hours waiting for other people to join the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this stage are you able to tell us about how many people were in this part of Kozarac in the triangle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 2 and a half to 3,000 people, men, women, children, old people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How were you being controlled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not control us. We were just waiting there so that we could all gather together, that people from other villages could come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was anyone giving orders to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an officer whom I do not know and we listened to what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you recognised anyone at all within the military during your progress down from [redacted] down to the triangle in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I recognised two boys.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Goran Borovnica and Zoran Sumar from Donji Orlovci, a neighbour of my wife's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In your movement through Kozarac, had you seen Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you had passed through Kozarac, were you able to see what damage had been done to the town caused by the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in a position to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what that was, what the town looked like then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not badly damaged. A couple of houses were just damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we see photographs of Kozarac today, we see virtually every house with holes for windows, no roof and enormous damage to the buildings. Were the buildings like that then or did that happen later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That happened later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the triangle, you told us that there were this large number of people. Did there come a time when you moved from there and the convoy started off to go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the column stayed there for about one and a half to two hours and then we moved towards the crossroads, Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. If we return then back to our map, and again if the overhead projector could be switched on? Put your pointer back on the triangle and show us then the route that you took to the intersection of the Banja Luka/Prijedor highway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that route take you past the saw mill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then having got to the intersection, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went in the direction of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you can just move your pointer along that so we can see on the map which particular road that is? Yes, if you just move it along the Prijedor highway? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Having then moved along the Prijedor highway, did there come a time when the column stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were stopped at Susici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What happened at Susici when the column stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were attacked from the trees. Muslims shot at the column of civilians from the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which part of Susici did the column stop at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Near the bus stop, just in front of the bridge, about 50 metres away from the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the column eventually move from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when this attack waned, we went on to towards Ziko's inn in Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About what time did you reach Ziko's inn in Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 1 o'clock, 1.30. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What happened there at Ziko's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were buses waiting for transport of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What happened to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing. I got on the bus. I did not know where I was going.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have to wait for any period of time at Ziko's before you were put on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we waited maybe half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So about what time was it that your bus left Ziko's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it must have been about 2.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, had more people joined that column, do you know, since it had left the triangle in Kozarac and moved along the highway towards Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You had moved in this column of people starting at [redacted] down to this place, Ziko's tavern. Were the people within that column frightened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did people know what was going to happen to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they did not know what was going to happen. I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were put on the bus, did you know where you were going to be taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where did that bus take you? Where did you end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trnopolje, the collection point at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your wife and other members of your family had been with you in your house [redacted] when the shelling started. Had you remained together as a group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you all go as a group to Trnopolje or were you split up and others taken to other places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all went Trnopolje, and then from Trnopolje we went to Prijedor to stay with family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long were you at Trnopolje camp for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe two or three hours I stayed there -- three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that you then stayed elsewhere, having been in Trnopolje for that period of time. Whereabouts did you go and stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Donji Orlovci [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At any stage during your movement and progress from [redacted] to this time when you are in Trnopolje, did you see Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned seeing two young men in Kozarac whom you recognised, Zoran Sumar and Goran Borovnica. Can you recollect whereabouts in Kozarac you had seen either of them? First of all, Sumar, can you recollect where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I first saw Goran near the old school in Kozarac, that is, just below the Mutnik Mosque and then I saw Zoran about 50 metres later on the left-hand side at an intersection of roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which intersection of roads is that in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the road leading to Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can just have a look at Prosecution Exhibit which is Exhibit 196? It may show up better on this plan that I am going to put in front of you which is not a map in the same form that we have been looking at, witness, but is a plan that someone has drawn of Kozarac. (Handed). If we can have one put on the monitor as well so that it can be shown? You can see there the plan of Kozarac and can you see on the top right corner where the motel is marked? If you just put your pointer where that is.[redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see where the mosque is, that is Mutnik Mosque, down below?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it must be this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you indicated seeing Goran Borovnica near the school and near that area, can you indicate where that would be on this plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan] Here somewhere, about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will continue until quarter to 12, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am obliged, your Honour. (To the witness): When you left Trnopolje and went to live in Donji Orlovci, did you move out of the area at all of Donji Orlovci? Were you able to travel around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went to Prijedor. I did move around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After the conflict, can you remember the first time you met Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the conflict or after the conflict broke out? I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After the conflict, can you remember the first time you met Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe about one and a half or two months. I cannot exactly remember the date. It was about one and a half or two months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We met in Prijedor in front of the Rudnik restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that a meeting by accident or an arranged meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, by accident we met. It was a coincidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had a drink and we talked about Kozarac and ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you talk with him about the future of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you make any plans with him about the future for Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we spoke about returning to Kozarac, about living there and building it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had anyone started to rebuild Kozarac, as far as you know, at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The discussion you had with him, was it a discussion as to what you were going to do, how you were going to rebuild Kozarac, or was it just dreams of rebuilding Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spoke about Kozarac and two or three days later we went to the President of the Prijedor opstina to come to an agreement on the return to Kozarac and on clearing it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you go back to Kozarac yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was your first return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I think in the elementary school of Kozarac we had a meeting with the President of the opstina and all the citizens who had stayed behind in Kozarac. Whether it was the end of August or the beginning of September, I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was Dusko Tadic involved in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was his role?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was elected at the meeting as Secretary of the local community of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why was he elected as Secretary of the Local Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because he was the greatest supporter of returning to Kozarac, of bringing it back to life, of us continuing life there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who was the President of the Local Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am afraid I cannot -- I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had Dusko Tadic been involved in SDS politics, as far as you were aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was his appointment as Secretary of the Local Commune in Kozarac in any way to do because of political views or his political knowledge or his political associations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think it was the people of Kozarac, the inhabitants of Kozarac, who elected him because he was the man who most championed our return to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he made Secretary of the Local Commune because he had been involved in fighting in Kozarac and because he had been involved in activities involving the camps in opstina Prijedor? Was that anything to do with his election?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was the greatest supporter of returning to Kozarac and living there and that is why the people elected him. I know nothing about these other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you eventually return to Kozarac yourself to live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I and my wife, we returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About September we cleaned up our houses. Towards the end of September already we started living there, end of September, beginning of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see Dusko Tadic in Kozarac during this time, from the time of that meeting you referred to to the time afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would see him in Kozarac, in the Local Commune premises. We were cleaning up our homes and I would see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How did he spend his time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly he was in the school working in the Local Commune and assisting the people with their work. He would take people to their houses and accommodate them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There has been an assertion in evidence in this Court that later on in the year, in November/December 1992, he was Commander of Trnopolje camp. Could you see that? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I neither knew about it nor did I hear anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I mean, did any of his business, as you could see it, cause his involvement with Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, it did not, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be an appropriate moment. I am grateful for the Court allowing me to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have concluded my questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We thought, perhaps, Mr. Kay, that the witness (as we have followed in other procedures) can identify that he is the person, without revealing his name, of course, that he purports to be. We forgot to do that. You tell me how you would like to handle that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it may be appropriate if we, perhaps, did it on a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is how we have done it in the past. We have put a piece of paper in front of the witness and then confirmed that he is that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, attentive as ever, has already ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He is one step ahead of me, just waiting for me, just in case, Mr. Wladimiroff, OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Witness, could you confirm that that is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Without saying your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then you will show that to the Prosecutor, please. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I would also like to start with a piece of paper. Witness U, if you would, I would like to pass you a piece of paper with two names on it and I would like you to indicate whether that is the names of your wife and your son. I believe this will be Prosecution Exhibit 347, your Honour. If that could be shown to the Defence first, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You can take a look at it. We have not been offering the papers into evidence. If it does come into evidence, of course, it would have to be sealed. Do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There would be no objection to that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 347 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Witness U, you testified that the shelling went on for approximately three days in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That on that third day you then left with a column of people from the area of [redacted] and headed into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the fourth day, May 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated that when you went through you noted that the houses were not damaged very much, that the damage which is obvious in that town today was caused at some later time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You also testified that as you were moving through this column there was no one controlling you, none of the soldiers were controlling the column, but you indicated you were given some orders by an officer at the triangle. What were those orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The orders were in what direction to move in the column and how to move, that is, not to leave the column and to go altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the column? What were you told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why were people forming a column and leaving the town? What was the purpose of the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For safety sake, people were going to that collection centre, to a safe place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You testified that the houses, the buildings themselves, were not being destroyed by the shelling. So what was the safety concern? Why did people not simply return to their homes if they were not being destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the shelling, most houses that were damaged were towards the Prijedor/Banja Luka road. That is where most shells fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Fine, and so in those areas that were away from the Banja Luka/Prijedor road, why would those people have been compelled to leave their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, everybody was leaving and we had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When did this damage to all of these homes take place, this subsequent damage? When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I was not in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You testified earlier you returned to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I returned, I returned in August, early September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At the time that you returned to Kozarac, had all the damage been done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you were in this column you indicated that you saw Goran Borovnica near the old school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, is it not correct that when you saw Borovnica, you left the column, went over to Goran Borovnica, greeted him, shook his hand and had a conversation with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came up to the column and shook hands with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So he approached you, you did not approach him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he was the one who approached me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What kind of conversation did you have when he came up to the column and greeted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he asked me if my family was alive, where was my son, was he safe, whether my wife was with me and who was left behind in the village, some elderly women and people like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ask him why they were shelling the area around your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What about these other JNA soldiers that you said you saw, did you ask any of them what the purpose of the shelling was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did any of them tell you what the purpose of the shelling was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You said that when the column moved out on to the Banja Luka/Prijedor highway and headed towards Prijedor, there was an ambush, an attack, in which the column was fired on. You said that you were fired on by Muslims who fired on you from the trees. If these people were in the trees, how did you know they were Muslims who were doing the firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because the Serbs soldiers who were escorting us, our column, were responding to the attack and we simply all went into ditches waiting for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So how many Serb soldiers were with this column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the column was quite long. There could have been some 30 or 40 soldiers escorting the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How many people were wounded in this attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilians, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Anyone -- how many people in total were wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nobody was wounded there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit 280 shown to the witness, please? It might speed things up, your Honour, I have a copy of it here. (Handed). If that could be placed on the Elmo, please? If you could zoom into the area that you see marked on there, Mr. Usher, Kozarusa and Kozarac, if you could use the Elmo zoom to move in? Witness U, if you could, please, indicate to us on that map where approximately this ambush occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the plan]. It was here, about a kilometre, a kilometre, 500 metres towards Kozarusa at Susici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What side of the road did the firing come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you were heading towards Prijedor, OK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Prijedor, yes, on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: On the right side. So it would be between what is marked there as that red road, just above the word "Kozarusa" and where that yellow road is above it, the old Banja Luka/Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Susici there was the bus stop, Susici, that is the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes. So the firing was on that side of the road where the old Banja Luka/Prijedor road is as well, as you can see it on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You have indicated that these forces were in the trees. How far away were they from the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about 100 metres, 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Approximately, how many forces were there that attacked the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know. All we heard were shots and bullets falling on the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did the bullets fall in the part of the column that you were actually in or in a different part of the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We hid in a ditch. There was a deep ditch and that is where we hid and bullets flew over us to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You just said that the bullets were hitting the road, so were they hitting the road in the area where you were, where you had just left, or did they hit in a different area of the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There in the column where I was and other -- and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So how could you tell where the firing was coming from if you were down in the ditch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, from the right-hand side because the army, the soldiers, went there and rejected the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there that went and rejected this attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. About 20 or 30 soldiers went to the right towards those woods, towards those ponds. It lasted for about 10 minutes and then we started off again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you hear any artillery firing in response to this attack or any tank fire in response to this attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So in this attack of a column of civilians, no one was injured and the Serb forces who had all of that military equipment at their disposal responded only by a few of the men who were escorting the column, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You said that when you went to Trnopolje you were only there for two or three hours, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, you were taken out by [redacted] a policeman, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You then said that you went to Prijedor and then on to Donji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Donji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Until you returned to Kozarac in August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, September, rather, it was the end of September when I returned to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You said that during that time you travelled to Prijedor, correct, the time you lived in Donji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How did you get to Prijedor from Donji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By road, I walked on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How often did you go to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two or three times a week. I went to report to my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What company was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Which company were you reporting to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And you were still being paid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What route would you take to get to Prijedor from Donji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donji Orlovci, Orlovaca, Prijedor. There is an asphalt road there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we could look at that map again, please, on the monitor? If you could point out that map, that route, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the model].

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The area where you are pointing right now? Then you would follow that road which is a yellow road on the map? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This would be this route to Trnopolje, Donji Orlovci, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. When you went to that meeting in Kozarac you said that the meeting which you attended with Dusko Tadic, it was also attended by the President of the opstina of Prijedor. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was Milomir Stakic who was the Mayor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At this meeting where Dusko Tadic was elected as Secretary of the Local Commune, who attended this meeting? Who was present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The local people from Kozarac, from Podgradje, Babici, and from Kozarac, the people from Kozarac, the people who were there from ages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Which people were those? Do you remember their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, Bosko Dragicevic, Dane Basaraba, Gojko Baltic, all of them were there. Drago, Coprka, Bosko Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Those names you have just mentioned, they were all Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, the majority of the people at that meeting were Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Serbs, but there were also two or three Croat families.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who arranged this meeting with the President of the opstina, Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Dusko Tadic, Bosko Dragicevic, Dane Basaraba.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that because they were all members of the local SDS Council?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know about that. I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You live in Kozarac now, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The majority of the residents in Kozarac now are Serbs, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: During this time, after August/September '92, while you were attempting to develop plans to rebuild Kozarac, did you visit with and meet with Dusko Tadic in his coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because the coffee bar was not working after the attack and after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you meet him then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would meet in the school, in the office of the Local Commune, in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where was Dusko Tadic living at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was living at the time in Kozarac. He was sleeping in the school, in the Local Commune when the meetings were being held, when we were discussing the return to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was living in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where in Kozarac -- in your own house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In whose house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the house of a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Prior to the war -- what about the Muslim who had previously owned that house, do you know where he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, while you were living in that person's home, do you know where that person was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor, the daughter of the owner was living in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why were they not living in their own home in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because she got killed during the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Prior to the war you were a member of the Kozarac TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you a member of any Defence organisation in the area of [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated that your son was not at home when Kozarac was shelled when the attack started. Is that because two to three weeks prior to the war he, in fact, joined Serb military forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your son had not joined the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When did he join?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On July 2nd 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: As a consequence, you owed a lot of people money before the war, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Prior to the attack, a number of those people were always looking for you in order to get their money back, to be repaid, is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is it not true that you saw this war and, more importantly, being on the right side of this war as an opportunity to cancel all of your debts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never thought about it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, your thoughts went beyond that. Is it not correct that you and your wife then looted and stole [redacted] [redacted] including, for example, the property of Dzemal Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is it not true that your wife routinely accompanied the Serb forces around Prijedor to loot property and, in fact, her particular role was to search any women who were found in the homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A few matters in re-examination: you have just been asked questions about what you have described as the ambush on the column as it was on the Banja Luka/Prijedor highway. Did you actually see who was firing at the column? Did you see any of the people who were firing in your direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You referred to them as being in the trees, but did you actually know they were in the trees because that was something you were able to see or were you told that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told that the Muslims had attacked the column of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The people who told you this, were who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At about what time did this attack take place when you were on the highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, but about 11.30 or 12 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When the soldiers left to deal with the problem, as you told us, did any soldiers remain guarding you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you jumped into the ditch, was that as a result of an order from the soldiers or because there was firing towards the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The soldiers told us to lie down so that nobody would get injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So had the firing happened before you lay down and attempted to conceal yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, while we were still in the column the firing started and then the order came to lie down in the trenches, in the ditch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you see in which direction the soldiers went when you describe 20 or 30 of them moving away to the right-hand side of the road? Did you see where exactly they went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went in the direction of a thicket behind the column, behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any firing of weapons by those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether firing was being returned in any way towards the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the soldiers taking, from what you could see, evasive action? Were they trying to conceal themselves whilst they were going towards this thicket?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serb soldiers went and repulsed the attack and then they came back about 10 minutes later and joined the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about Kozarac and meetings of the Council. You were asked whether the coffee bar was a place which Dule Tadic owned, whether that was used for meetings. You said that it was not working. What had happened to Dusko Tadic's coffee bar? How was it at this time in August or September 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all broken up, demolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it a place that could be made to work as a coffee bar or was the damage too great at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The damage was too great. The windows were broken, the bar, the water pipes. It required a great deal of investment to be repaired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were also asked about the people who attended these meetings at this time. You said that a man called Stakic who was from Prijedor attended the first meeting. Did he attend other meetings of the Local Commune or was it just the first one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know about the other meetings because I was not there afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is all I ask in re-examination. Does your Honour have any questions?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated that the coffee bar was damaged during the attack and that the comment was made it would require a great deal of investment to fix it up, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact that coffee bar is now open and in fact it is one of the few businesses that is open in Kozarac, is that not also true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Tadic's coffee bar is not working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it the case that the former site of the Nipon cafe bar at the Tadic family home is, in fact, still closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The coffee bar of Dusko Tadic is closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Is there a bar now open at the family home that is in fact the other side of the building in a different position to the place where Dusko Tadic's cafe was previously positioned in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko's brother Mladen Tadic has opened a coffee bar in the same family home but on another side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that on the other side of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is in the same house. There is Dusko Tadic, then his brother Ljubo and then Mladen Tadic, and there are business premises one next to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And that is a new bar that has been opened by his brother Mladen, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, I had two or three questions to ask you. They all relate to the column and your movement down Marsala Tita Street. First of all, do I understand that you were moving with your wife, she was with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And any other members of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My uncle, his wife, my brother, his wife and other neighbours.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you moved down through the town, did you hear any shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard shooting above Kozarac, Brdjani, Arifagici, Besici, two or three kilometres from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: But you heard no shooting just close to the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you hear or see anyone called out from the column, any of the people who were moving in the column being told to leave the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You did not see any soldiers or anyone else pulling people out of the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column was long. It was a big one. I did not see anyone doing that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Then when you got to the buses you had to wait for some time before you got on to a bus and then before the bus moved off to Trnopolje. That is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see any process of separation of men from women at that stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Women were separated before, before Kozarusa, the women were separated from the men.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At what stage did that take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately after this ambush, about 10 minutes later, the women were separated from the men and taken away by buses.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And that means that your wife was taken away from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did she end up at Trnopolje where you were for some three or four hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she arrived first at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You joined her there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, by the time I got there she had already left to stay with [redacted] in Donji Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I see, and you followed on then, did you, from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us how many of the people in the column walking down Marsala Tita Street were Serbs and Croatians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A few were Serbs and Croats. The majority were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did they represent a significant number of the population of Serbs and Croatians in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the majority population of Kozarac were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Where did the Serbs go, if you know, before this march began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were they in town? Were they in Kozarac, as best as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not in Kozarac on May 27th when I left.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You do not know where they went?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: They just left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, some -- I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know when the Serbs left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you boarded the buses, Judge Stephen was asking you some questions about the separating of men and women before you got to that point, or you said it happened before you got to that point. When you boarded the buses did you see Goran Borovnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You testified that as you were coming down the column when you were in Kozarac there were Yugoslav soldiers controlling the column, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And that you saw Goran Borovnica and another individual. What was his name, Zoran -- what was his name, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Sumar.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were they part of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time it was the JNA, the Yugoslav Army. Later on it was transformed into the army of the Republika Srspka.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Well, how would you characterise the army then when they were escorting the column? What would you call them: JNA, Yugoslav Army, Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would rather call them the Army of the Republika Srspka.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Goran Borovnica and Zoran Sumar, the other gentleman, were they part of the Republic Srpske's army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.
