utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see any individuals then who were not part of the army as you were coming down that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I only saw soldiers who were before JNA and then they were transformed into the Army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was Goran Borovnica a part of the forces that were escorting the column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was going towards the Mutnik Mosque. He stayed there and we went on.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That day did you see anyone as you were coming down the column, other than Goran Borovnica and Zoran, who were not part of the group of soldiers who were escorting the column, if you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw soldiers, but I did not know the names of those soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So everyone you saw was a soldier except Goran Borovnica and Zoran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Goran and Zoran were also soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: OK. The house that you are living in now, in response to questions I think from Mr. Keegan you said that the woman, the daughter of the family, moved to Prijedor and then at some point you said that she was killed. Were you talking about the same person? Was it the daughter of the family who lived in the house that you are in now? Is it the daughter who was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How did you happen to come to live in that house? Did you buy it from someone or how did you happen, you and your family, to come to live in this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not buy it. I was given it by the Prijedor opstina.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What happened to your house in [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was destroyed during the operations, war operations.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were many houses destroyed in [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: By shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. After we left on May 27th I did not go back up for four or five months.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I thought you testified there was some shelling but very little and it was accidental. That may not have been in [redacted]; that may have been somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In [redacted] there was little shelling at the time until May 27th. I left and then I did not go back for four or five months.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Then when you went back did you find that there had been significant damage to the homes there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Most of the homes were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you returned to Kozarac in September, I think you said August -- no, you said the end of September of 1992, were there any Muslims living in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac, no.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Also you testified that Mr. Tadic was elected secretary to the Local Council, and then at one point one of the lawyers used the word "appointed". So it is not clear to me whether Mr. Tadic was elected or appointed secretary of the Local Council. Was there a vote taken or did someone appoint him to the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We citizens elected him as secretary of the Local Commune.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What citizens? Was it a ballot taken for all of the citizens in Kozarac or who was it who was voting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people who had returned to Kozarac and the people from the surrounding villages, Babici, Balte, Yaruga, they were there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just one your Honour or it may be two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the name of the person who owned this home that you now live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Santa Nedzod.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How was he killed and where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I did not hear that he was killed nor do I know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated that the person who had lived in the home had been killed, and you said a woman earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who in the opstina Prijedor gave you this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Prijedor opstina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who did you have to go to to get permission to have this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And where was this commission? Did you have to go into Prijedor or did you go through the Local Commune in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Assembly of the Prijedor opstina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you yourself go and ask permission for this particular house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it went through the Local Commune, and the opstina issued decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So was that through Dusko Tadic that you went to get this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was a commission with Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: He was a member of that commission as the secretary of the Local Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the witness being permanently excused, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Sir, you are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you very much for coming. You should keep your seat for a moment and the Judges will leave. We will stand in recess for lunch until 2.35. (1.05 p.m.).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
